item.title: CHIPS Alliance at 2026 OCP Global Summit
item.description:
2026 OCP Global Summit, themed “Scaling Innovation for the AI Era,” will be held October 12-15 in San Jose, California. The event brings together industry leaders, researchers, and members of the open compute community to share technical progress, address emerging challenges, and advance efficient, scalable, and sustainable open hardware and software.

Several sessions relate to the CHIPS Alliance Caliptra and VeeR projects, covering silicon roots of trust, device identity, secure key distribution, design verification, streaming boot, package-aware integrity and package-granular attestation, manageability, and certificate refresh. Speakers represent CHIPS Alliance member organizations including AMD, Google, Intel, lowRISC, Marvell, Microsoft, NVIDIA, and Research Institutes of Sweden.

item.title: The Future is Open (and AI-Assisted)- Highlights from the Open-Source EDA Birds-of-a-Feather Session at DAC 2026
item.description:
By: Dr. Yiting Liu, UC San Diego

The energy at DAC 2026 in Long Beach was palpable during the seventh annual Open-Source EDA Birds-of-a-Feather (BoF) session. This fast-paced Tuesday evening forum gathered academic researchers, industry practitioners, and open-source developers to discuss the transformative intersection of AI, open-source hardware, and open-source EDA. As the lines between traditional EDA and agentic AI blur, the session proved that the open-source EDA community is more active and essential than ever.

item.title: CHIPS Alliance at the DAC 2026 Open Source EDA Birds-of-a-Feather Session
item.description:
CHIPS Alliance will participate in the “Open-Source EDA, Data and Collaboration” Birds-of-a-Feather session at DAC 2026 on Tuesday, July 28, at the Long Beach Convention Center.

The seventh in a series that began at DAC 2018, the BoF will bring together academic researchers, industry practitioners, and open source maintainers for rapid-fire presentations, dedicated Q&A panels, and networking opportunities. The broader program will cover AI-assisted EDA, open source ecosystem governance, robust PDK development, open source AMS design flows, benchmarking, industrial usage, and workforce development.
